cut.description: Whether every node cuts the user now, because the total reached the quota.

total_bytes.description: The sum over the counted nodes, in the user's current period.

allow.description: The classes besides `cover` that the operator allows: no_cover, exposed, plain.

exit.description: The provider's exit to leave through. Left out: the provider's default.

name.description: The exit's display name. Defaults to the tag.

profile.description: The profile of the provider to use. Left out: the first one the node would use.

tag.description: The tag of the upstream in the node's config, and of the exit that leaves through it: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, - and _.

last_login.description: The last login, from the audit log. None when the log holds none.

totp_used.description: Whether a code from the current TOTP secret has been used, which says the admin set up their authenticator. False after a reset until the next login.

action.description: enable, disable, delete, reset_usage, reset_links, add_group, remove_group, set_quota, set_expiry, set_device_limit or set_exits.

remove_devices.description: For reset_links: remove the devices that were enrolled with the old links.

value.description: The group name, the quota (an object with quota_bytes and quota_period), the expiry in Unix seconds or null, the device limit, or the exits ("all" or a list of exit tags). A default exit the new exits leave out is cleared.

devices_removed.description: The devices removed by reset_links, null for the other actions.

Choice.description: The body of an update request.

revision.description: The revision the change was made on, which the node checks as If-Match.
The revision the node's config was last read at, which the change is applied on.

typed.description: The eight groups the other operator reads out. Typing this side's own does not confirm.

Counts.description: How many requests each kind of refusal turned away since the start, and how many were served.

full.description: Requests turned away because the gateway's memory of acted requests was full.

key_origin.description: "device" when the device made its key, "panel" when the panel did. The second is the weaker choice: the private key sits in the panel's database and travels in the document.

token_gen.description: The link generation the device enrolled with.

passphrase.description: At least 12 characters. It cannot be recovered: a backup without it is useless.

Endpoint.description: One subscription endpoint the panel answers on and puts in links.

name.description: 1 to 64 characters of a-z, 0-9, dash and underscore.

pins.description: SHA-256 of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo of the endpoint's certificate, standard base64, at most two. Required for a self-signed certificate (an IP address as host). Empty for a chain-validated or plain endpoint. `https` only.

url.description: The public URL: `https`, or `http` for a plain endpoint, which hides nothing from the network (the exchange stays sealed). At most 256 characters, no fragment. The operator's web server forwards this host and path to the panel's `sub_path` followed by a slash and the name of the endpoint, and that path is how the panel knows which endpoint a request reached.

assigned.description: Of those, the ones given this endpoint by name.

plain.description: A plain http endpoint: the network can tell that the app is used, now and later in its records. The exchange itself stays sealed.

still_here.description: Accounts that resolve to another endpoint now and refreshed on this one in the last 30 days: moved, and not there yet. The endpoint can be retired when this is none.

users.description: Accounts whose links and documents use this endpoint, by the resolution.

file.description: The same as the content of a file the client imports.

link.description: A whole signed document in a link, when it is small enough for one. Null otherwise.

files.description: Files in the folder, real and decoy together. Null before the first round.

path.description: The folder to copy to the host: a link that is switched to each new round in one step.

shared_host.description: False when the host is not on the panel's list of shared host names: a censor that learns it can block it without blocking anything else.

size.description: The size of every file of the folder, in bytes. Null before the first round.

written_at.description: When this folder was last written.

accounts_without_device.description: Accounts with no device yet: they hold a link made under some key and have not imported it.

affected.description: Accounts that sent a request under a key stolen earlier and whose tokens are not reset yet.

clock_synchronized.description: Whether the system reports its clock as synchronized, null when it cannot tell. The gateway needs a synchronized clock.

loaded.description: False while the keys are lost or unreadable: the endpoint answers every request as an unknown path.

switch_due.description: The active key is older than 180 days.

public_key.description: The WireGuard public key of the inbound.

transport_public_key.description: The public half of the node transport key. Null when the inbound has none.

cert.description: As on create: needed for vless and trojan, refused for shadowsocks.

decoy.description: For vless and trojan. The inbound's own decoy stays when left out.

host.description: The host the links name. Empty or left out for the node's first public address.

listen.description: The address Xray listens on. 0.0.0.0 when left out.

new_server_key.description: For shadowsocks: a new server key. Every share link of the inbound holds the old one, so every user needs a new link.

cert.description: Paths of the certificate and key files on the node. Needed for vless and trojan, refused for shadowsocks.

decoy.description: For vless and trojan, the origin of the operator's own web server (http://127.0.0.1:8080) that anything that is not a user's connection is handed to. Taken from the node's `tls` transport when left out; the inbound is refused when the node has none.

host.description: The host the links name, in the place of the node's first public address.

listen.description: The address Xray listens on. 0.0.0.0 when left out.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the provider's signing key, as 8 groups of 4 hex digits. The provider can read it out for comparison.

host.description: The host and port of the provider's endpoint. This is where the node will connect.

fingerprint.description: First 16 bytes of the SHA-256 of the key, as the apps show it.

qr_svg.description: The same link as an SVG QR code.

veilway.description: The link in the form providers hand out. A secret: it is shown to the one who asked and stored nowhere but in the sealed copy.

Live.description: What the last poll saw, for the pages that show the node now.

exits.description: Every exit with its state: whether its proxy relays UDP, whether its interface is up, whether its link is up.

health.description: Version, uptime, generation, flows and the counters that say the node is unwell.

proxies.description: What each proxy inbound (`socks5`, `http`, `mixed`) counted since the node started: connections opened and open now, logins and connections refused, and the bytes carried, under `name`, the inbound's tag. As the node reports them.

rates.description: Rates in bytes per second over the node's window, by user, inbound, exit and outbound.

tunnels.description: What each tunnel of the node counted since the node started: connections or sessions opened and open now, those refused by reason, and the bytes carried. As the node reports them.

password_change_required.description: True when two-step sign-in is off and this admin's password is shorter than 12 characters: only the password change works until it is done.

totp.description: Not read while two-step sign-in is off.

dry_run.description: Only count: say who moves and who stays, and change nothing.

endpoint.description: The endpoint to move to. Null takes the accounts' own choice away (they follow their group or the default), or the group's.

group.description: The group to move: sets the endpoint of the group, which every member without an endpoint of their own follows.

users.description: The accounts to move: one, a selection or many. Give this or `group`.

hosts.description: Take the refresh hosts the node reported as pending.

move.description: Follow the move of the provider's endpoint the node reported as pending.

changes_check.description: Of those who move, the ones whose endpoint is checked another way at the new one (chain, pins or plain http), which the app says when it asks.

moving.description: Accounts whose endpoint changes. Their next document names the new endpoint, and the app asks its user once.

staying.description: Accounts the request names (or the group holds) whose endpoint stays.

to_plain.description: Of those who move, the ones moving to a plain http endpoint.

allowed_sources.description: Source addresses the token works from. Empty means any.

scope.description: "read" (reads only), "users" (users, devices and links) or "full" (everything an API token may do).

on_host.description: The file of the next key's private half is still on this host. Whoever takes the active key from the host takes the next one with it: move the file away.

link.description: The tag of a link of node 1 that node 1 manages (`manage: "peer"`), made by the link pairing. A link already bound to a node is refused.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters, without spaces around it.

pool_v4.description: The IPv4 range devices get their address at this node from.

clock_synchronized.description: Whether the system reports its clock as synchronized, null when it cannot tell. A panel whose clock is off by more than a day writes static mirror names that no client asks for.

gateway_missing.description: True while no gateway key can be read: the subscription endpoint answers every request as an unknown path.

gateway_switch_due.description: The active gateway key is older than 180 days: time to load the next key.

behind.description: Whether its users are still to be pushed.

counted.description: Whether what the node counts adds to the users' totals.

devices.description: The devices that have an address in its pool.

down_since.description: Since when the link has not been up, Unix seconds, null while it is.

link.description: The tag of the link of node 1 that reaches the node. Null for node 1.

link_state.description: The state of that link as node 1 reports it, null for node 1 or when node 1 cannot say.

max_rate.description: The most the node's counters may grow, in bytes per second. Null is the default of 1.25 GB/s.

pool_v4.description: The address pool devices get their address at this node from.

relays.description: The relays of this node, with the rules of node 1's. Each subscription carries them on this node's profiles for the accounts they reach, as node 1's are carried on its own.

slug.description: Short and lowercase, put in front of this node's profile ids.

wanted_rev.description: The revision of what the panel wants the node to have, and the last one the node took. A node whose applied revision is lower is behind.

counted.description: False stops its usage from adding to the users' totals, for a node that reports false usage. Its users stay on it.

max_rate.description: The most its counters may grow, in bytes per second, or null for the default.

pool_v4.description: Only for a remote node that no device has an address at yet: node 1's pool is the `pool_v4` setting.

relays.description: The relays of this remote node, which node 1's own rules check. Each one's addresses reach the profiles of this node for the accounts it names, by id or by group, or for everyone when it names neither. Node 1's relays are set in the settings.

NodeState.description: Whether the node took the change. The panel's database is changed either way and the next successful push brings the node up to date.

counted.description: Whether it counts toward the user's total. An admin can stop counting a node.

reported_at.description: When the panel last read it. Unix seconds.

used_bytes.description: What the node counts now in the user's period, and what it counted before it restarted.

NotFound.description: What the endpoint (and every path the panel does not serve) answers to a request it will not take. The operator copies it from the web server in front, see "The endpoint" on the subscription format page.

direction.description: "forward" or "reverse". In a forward link this node is the exit.

inbound.description: The tag of the `veilway` inbound the link connects to.

inbound_public_key.description: The inbound's WireGuard public key, as `/links/inbounds` reports it.

listener.description: A reverse link and a managed link: this node's link address, one for each family of `dialler`.

managed.description: This node manages the other node through the link. The other node is told so before it agrees, and `listener` is then required.

tag.description: The tag the link gets in this node's config.

transport_public_key.description: Needed when `transports` lists tls or ws.

transports.description: The transports the other node is offered, in the shape of a profile's `transports`.

set.description: Members that replace the derived ones, such as `inbound_public_key`, `name` or `transports`. An empty object clears the override.

Part.description: What an update request is for. The word is what the host script reads.

accept.description: Must be true: the operator has seen where this node would dial and agrees.

managed.description: True when the offer makes this node the one that manages the other node. It must say what the offer says.

tag.description: The tag the link gets in this node's config.

user.description: The account whose documents are shown. Null shows what accounts without a relay of their own get.

allow_private.description: Whether the node may dial private addresses the profiles name. Default false.

link.description: The native `veilway://sub/` link of the provider.

via.description: The tag of a direct or socks5 outbound the node reaches the provider through. Left out: from the node itself.

private_addresses.description: Private addresses the profile names to dial.

rating.description: "protected", "detectable" or "unsafe": what a censor can see, worked out by the node.

refused.description: Why this node would not use the profile under the settings of the preview. Null when it would.

transports.description: Transport types in the provider's order.

password.description: A secret: it is sent in the clear on the way in to a proxy inbound, and is stored sealed.

username.description: The name of the account, which is the proxy user name.

totp.description: Not read while two-step sign-in is off.

confirm.description: Must be true: making new keys on a panel that has accounts means old links do not open at a first import, and clients learn the new key only from a newer document on a static mirror or from a link shown again.

Relay.description: A forwarder on another address that passes bytes to the node unchanged: nginx `stream`, a DNAT rule, HAProxy, or a content delivery network. TLS, the proofs and WireGuard run end to end through it, so it sees nothing and cannot pass for the node.

address.description: An IP address, or a host name such as a content delivery network's, which each document turns into the addresses it has then: apps dial candidates by address, never by name.

groups.description: Groups whose accounts get it. Empty with `users` too means everyone gets it.

inbound_ports.description: The relay's port per inbound and transport type, keyed `<inbound tag>/<type>`. It wins over `ports`. Every transport of that type in the inbound gets it: two of one type in an inbound share the web port or the address anyway. A key naming no inbound or transport of the node is ignored.

inbounds.description: The tags of the `veilway` inbounds it carries. Empty for all of them.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters, unique among the relays.

ports.description: The relay's port per transport type, where it is not the node's own port.

prefer.description: Put its candidates before the node's own address instead of after it.

transports.description: The transport types it carries: udp, udp-obfs, tls, ws, fronted, fronted-shaped. Empty for all of them.

users.description: Accounts that get it, by id. Empty with `groups` too means everyone gets it.

confirmed.description: Whether the provider took the word that the device left. False: its place stays until the provider removes it. Null: the node never ran this upstream, so there was nothing to tell.

count.description: Accounts whose token is reset, or would be.

links.description: The new links, when applied. A secret, shown once.

dry_run.description: Only count the accounts and change nothing.

remove_devices.description: Remove the devices that were enrolled with the old link. They are listed in the answer either way.

saved_as.description: The folder in the data directory that holds the database and keys this restore replaced.

warnings.description: Things the operator should read before the panel comes back: the gateway keys on the host were not the backup's.

accounts.description: Accounts that ever sent a request under it.

accounts_recent.description: Accounts that sent a request under this key in the last 30 days.

Review.description: What the provider's document holds, verified by the node under the key of the link. It names no key and no secret.

allow_private.description: Filled in by the panel: whether the node may dial private addresses of the profiles under this preview.

classes.description: The classes the profiles list. The operator consents to each besides `cover`.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the key the document is signed with, which is the one in the link.

host.description: Filled in by the panel: the host and port of the provider's endpoint, as the link names them.

link.description: The user's current link in the `veilway` form, for a link the panel keeps no copy of: one just made, or any link when the panel shows links once. It has to be the user's current token. Left out, the panel opens its own sealed copy.

password.description: At least 10 characters. It locks the file and the panel keeps no copy of it, so it cannot be recovered. Send it another way than the file.

value.description: The new content of the section: an object for routing, dns, log and replay, a list for the others. A change to `replay.cache` takes effect at the node's next start.

password_change_required.description: True when two-step sign-in is off and this admin's password is shorter than 12 characters: only the password change works until it is done.

Settings.description: What an operator sets once for the whole panel.

default_endpoint.description: The name of the default endpoint. Empty only while there are no endpoints.

endpoints.description: The named subscription endpoints, at most 16, each on its own host and port and each reached by its own path, the panel's `sub_path` and the endpoint's name. An account's links and documents use the endpoint resolved for it: its own, else the first of its groups that has one in `group_endpoints`, else the default.

faketls_keys.description: The public half of the key of each `faketls` transport, by inbound tag and listen address. The node shows a key only as a marker once it holds it, so the panel makes the public half when the key is applied in full. Owned by the server: read-only in the API, and a settings update keeps the stored value whatever it carries.

gateway_retired_days.description: Days a retired gateway key keeps opening requests after a routine switch, 30 to 365.

group_endpoints.description: The endpoint of a group, by group name.

idle_device_days.description: Devices that have not refreshed for this many days are removed, which frees their places: an app that was uninstalled, or a phone that was lost. 0 keeps them. A device whose key the panel made never refreshes and is never removed this way.

inbound_keys.description: The public half of the key of each `veilway` inbound, by inbound tag, which its profile is made with. Made the same way as `faketls_keys`, and read-only in the API too.

inbound_ranges.description: The IPv4 range of each `veilway` inbound, by inbound tag, as it was when the profiles were published. A document gives a device the address it has inside the range of the profile's inbound. Written by publish.

new_devices.description: How many new devices one subscription link may enroll in any window of `new_devices_window_minutes` minutes, 1 to 64, which slows down a leaked link. The device limit still holds. A large count with a short window comes close to no limit.

new_devices_window_minutes.description: The length of the window of `new_devices`, 1 to 1440 minutes. It slides: a device that enrolled leaves the count that many minutes later.

node_host.description: The public host or address of this node, which the profiles' endpoints are made with.

node_poll_secs.description: How often the panel adds up the usage of each other server, in seconds, 10 to 600.

not_found.description: What the endpoint answers to a request it will not take, instead of the config file's. Null keeps the file's.

pool_v4.description: The address pool devices get their tunnel address from, an IPv4 network.

profile_overrides.description: Edits to the profiles derived from the node's inbounds, by inbound tag: an object whose members replace the derived ones.

profiles.description: One profile per inbound, in the shape of "A profile" on the subscription format page, without `device`. The panel adds the device.

published_relays.description: The relays as they were when the profiles were published. A document carries the ones that reach its account.

refresh_mirrors.description: Other endpoints of the same subscription, put in every document as `refresh_urls`. A string, or an object with `url` and `pins`.

relay_profiles.description: The profiles derived from an inbound that carry the published relays reaching each account, by profile id and inbound tag. Written by publish.

relays.description: Forwarders in front of the node. Each one adds its address to the candidates of the transports it carries when profiles are derived.

show_links_once.description: Store no copy of a token: a link is shown at creation and reset, and never again.

static_interval.description: Hours between publishing rounds of the static mirrors, 1 to 12.

static_mirrors.description: Base URLs of static mirrors, put in every document as `static_mirrors`: plain file hosting that holds each device's sealed document. `https`, a path ending in `/`, no pins and no IP literal, at most 4, and none shares host and port with the endpoint or a relay mirror.

subscription_notices.description: Notices put in every document as `notices`, at most 4. Apps keep them from their last refresh and show them with no connection, which the notices a node sends over the tunnel cannot do. A notice with the same text as one the node sends is shown once.

terms_url.description: The provider's own terms and privacy policy, put in every document as its `agreement`, which the apps ask users to accept. An `https` URL, or empty for none.

transport_clocks.description: When the first transport key of each `veilway` inbound and of each `ws-plain` transport (named as in `transport_keys`) became first, the key held second, the keys destroyed and where its rotation stands. Owned by the server: read-only in the API.

transport_key_days.description: Days the first transport key of a `veilway` inbound stays first before the panel makes a new one, 7 to 30 (a `ws-plain` transport's key at most 7). The node then holds the two keys, the old one second, and the old key keeps working for one more period of this length before it is destroyed.

transport_keys.description: The public half of the first transport key of each `veilway` inbound, by inbound tag, which its profile carries as `transport_public_key` for its `tls`, `ws` and `fronted` transports, and of each of its `ws-plain` transports (own keys), by tag, a newline and the path. Made the same way as `inbound_keys`.

usage_poll_secs.description: How often the panel adds up node 1's usage, in seconds, 10 to 600.

error.description: Why the last round published nothing, if it failed.

start_id.description: Different on every start of the server.

two_step.description: False when the panel's config file turns the authenticator code off. Read-only: no route changes it.

SubNotice.description: A notice of the signed document: one line of plain text of at most 280 bytes, and the same line in other languages.

text.description: The default text, shown when no translation fits the app's language.

translations.description: At most 8 translations by language tag (`fa`, `de`, `pt-BR`, `zh-Hans`), each as long as `text` may be.

can_show.description: Whether the panel holds a sealed copy, so the link can be shown again. False with "show links once".

endpoint_url.description: The URL of the endpoint the account's links use now, empty while none is set.

key_fingerprints.description: Fingerprints of the current signing keys, which are not secret.

confirm.description: Only while no key file is on this host: must be true. Loading a key from the operator's hands makes it the active key, so this is the explicit yes.

id.description: Only while no key file is on this host: the id the supplied key had (the number the key carried in the links and documents, as the panel showed it before the file was lost). The key becomes the active one under that id.

private.description: The private half of the next key, 43 characters of base64url. Left out, the panel reads it from its `gateway_next` file.

affected.description: Accounts that sent a request under a stolen key (for a theft only): their tokens are to be reset.

next_file_written.description: False when the file for the new next key could not be written, so the shown key is the only copy.

next_private.description: The private half of the new next key. Shown once: move it away from this host and keep it. The panel keeps no copy except the file named in its config, which it lists as still on the host until the file is moved.

token.description: Shown once. Only its hash is stored.

totp_secret.description: Base32, for an authenticator app. Shown once, whatever two-step sign-in is set to.

TransportClock.description: Where the rotation of one transport slot stands. A slot holds at most two keys, and a rotation puts the fresh one first and keeps the current one second, so the old key lives one more period.

dropped.description: Public halves of keys the node destroyed, newest last and at most 16. A settings form that was loaded before a rotation may bring one back, and it is rewritten to the current key.

next.description: The public half of the key a rotation is putting in force, written before the node is asked so that a rotation the node took is finished later.

old_marker.description: The node's marker of the key that was first when a rotation began. Markers last as long as the node's process. When the node took the rotation but its answer was lost, it holds that marker second, which tells the next pass to finish the rotation.

previous.description: The public half of the key the node holds second, or empty when none is known. It is destroyed by the next rotation, so no profile may carry it.

public.description: The public half of the first key when the clock started. A first key that differs was changed by hand, which restarts the clock.

since.description: Unix time the key became first.

started.description: Unix time `next` was written, or 0 when no rotation waits. A rotation that is still not confirmed 2 days later is given up.

can_update.description: Whether the folder for update requests exists, which a host installed or updated by `veilway.sh` has.

latest.description: The newest release, when it is newer than this panel.

node_current.description: The node's version, when the node is reachable and reports one.

node_latest.description: The newest node release, when it is newer than the node's version.

node_updating.description: A node update was requested and the node has not come back with another version yet.

updating.description: A panel update was requested and this panel has not come back as another version yet.

Upstream.description: What the node is doing for one upstream.

notices.description: What the provider says to the device, as plain text.

pending_hosts.description: Refresh hosts that wait for the operator.

pending_move.description: A move of the provider's endpoint that waits for the operator.

reason.description: Plain words for why the state is what it is. Empty while it is up.

own.description: The endpoint given to the account by name, null when its group's or the default applies.

relays.description: The relays of the saved list that reach the account, by name: its own first, then its groups', then everyone's. A relay may still skip some of its inbounds or transports.

resolved.description: The endpoint in use for the account, null while no endpoint is set.

endpoint.description: The name of one of the settings' endpoints, or null for the group's or the default.

exit.description: One of the user's exits, or null for the node's default.

nodes.description: The ids of the nodes the user may use, at least one. Left out or null: every node.

device_limit.description: 0 is no limit beyond the node's own 16.

endpoint.description: The endpoint given to the user by name, null when the group's or the default applies. The one in use is at `/users/{id}/endpoint`.

exit.description: The exit the user's devices leave through when they choose none. Null is the node's default.

exits.description: "all" or a list of exit tags.

node.description: The node's own record of the user: usage, denial and traffic. Null when the node cannot be reached.

nodes.description: The ids of the nodes the user may use. Left out when every node is allowed.

proxy_login.description: Whether the user has a proxy password. The password itself is only at `/users/{id}/proxy/show`.

usage.description: What the nodes counted together, in a panel with more than one node. Only on one user's answer.

endpoint.description: The name of one of the settings' endpoints, or null for the group's or the default.

exit.description: One of the user's exits, or null for the node's default. A default the new exits leave out is cleared.

nodes.description: The ids of the nodes the user may use, at least one, or null for every node. A node taken out frees the addresses of the user's devices in its pool.

content.description: A wg-quick file. It holds the device's private key.

file_name.description: A name for the file: the account, the device and, when there is more than one file, the inbound.

inbound.description: The tag of the node's `wireguard` inbound the file connects to.

certificate_missing.description: A vless or trojan inbound without certificate files, which the node refuses.

decoy.description: The origin of the web server a stranger is handed to, for vless and trojan.

managed.description: Whether the panel made this inbound and holds its credentials, which links need.

own_host.description: The host the panel was given for this inbound, empty when links name the node's address.

link.description: A secret, like the subscription link.

qr_svg.description: The same link as an SVG QR code.

info.description: HTTP and JSON under the panel's path prefix. A browser logs in and sends the CSRF token on every change. An integration sends an API token as a Bearer header. The x-access member of an operation says what it needs: read, users or full are token scopes, session and session-reauth are for a logged-in admin only, and public needs nothing.
info.title: Veilway panel API

400.description: The request is malformed or breaks a rule.

401.description: Not logged in, or the token is not valid.

403.description: Not allowed: wrong scope, missing CSRF token or a re-authentication is due.

post.summary: Changes the password and ends every other session.

400.description: The request is malformed or breaks a rule.

401.description: Not logged in, or the token is not valid.

403.description: Not allowed: wrong scope, missing CSRF token or a re-authentication is due.

post.summary: Makes a new TOTP secret and ends every other session.

400.description: The request is malformed or breaks a rule.
